Hello Dejair, this is Svetlana Orlova from Kazan. We met on the last day of the congress, at the coffee break after the workshop on nerve pain. I am sorry it took me a week to reach out. I have two things for you. First, the paper I mentioned. I will forward it to you today, and if you cannot open the file, just tell me and I will send you a link. Second, my team is writing a proposal for a joint study on sensory loss, and we need a partner in Brazil. If you are interested, we can have a short video call next month. Please send me your availability for the first two weeks of November. If I do not hear from you, I will send you a reminder, because I really hope we can stay in touch. Thank you, and have a good week.

Here is my advice for every young researcher after a congress. Most contacts die in the first week. You meet twenty people, you collect twenty cards, and if you do nothing, nobody remembers you after a month. So I follow a simple rule. If I meet someone interesting, I write to them in the first forty-eight hours. The message is short: where we met, what we talked about, and one concrete offer. For example: if you send me your data, I will compare it with ours. Always attach something useful, like a paper, a slide or a link. People answer when you give them something first. And if they do not get back to you, do not take it personally. Researchers are busy. Wait ten days and send one friendly reminder. After that, let it go. Only one contact in five becomes a collaboration, but one is enough to change your career.
